title: Bayesian Attention Mechanism: A Probabilistic Framework for Positional Encoding and Context Length Extrapolation
claim: Different positional priors correspond to distinct distributions over past positions; a generalized prior can express and unify all of them.
layout: 1 panel, line plot over token positions, shaded masked region, legend inset
description: A single line plot with token positions ("this is a long context for the LLM <EOS>") on the x-axis and prior probability p_pos(i,j) on the y-axis. A vertical gray line marks the query position at the token "for". Everything to its right is shaded gray as masked future tokens. Four curves are drawn. The red causal mask is flat, then drops to zero at the query. The green ALiBi (Laplace) curve rises toward the query in a peaked, exponential shape. The pink GGD-BAM curve with β in (0,1) is a flatter, similarly peaked curve. The thick black GGD-BAM curve with β<0 is high at the distant past, drops to zero in the middle, then rises again. A legend box in the upper right names the curves. The eye goes first to the thick black curve.
caption: Visual comparison of different positional priors $\spgpos$ in BAM. Each curve represents the distribution over past token positions for a fixed query $\squery$ in a fixed token position $i$.
abstract: Transformer-based language models rely on positional encoding (PE) to handle token order and support context length extrapolation. However, existing PE methods lack theoretical clarity and rely on limited evaluation metrics to substantiate their extrapolation claims. We propose the Bayesian Attention Mechanism (BAM), a theoretical framework that formulates positional encoding as a prior within a probabilistic model. BAM unifies existing methods (e.g., NoPE and ALiBi) and motivates a new Generalized Gaussian positional prior that substantially improves long-context generalization. Empirically, BAM enables accurate information retrieval at $500\times$ the training context length, outperforming previous state-of-the-art context length generalization in long context retrieval accuracy while maintaining comparable perplexity and introducing minimal additional parameters.
